entities.summary: Josef Hlouch was a Czech Roman Catholic prelate and theologian who served as the Bishop of Budweis from 1947 until his death. Hlouch first served as a parish priest and professor in Olomouc and other places before he was appointed to the episcopate following a standoff between ecclesial authorities and the Nazis as to whom would assume the Budweis episcopal see. He was installed in his new diocese at a time when communist authorities solidified their control over the then-Czechoslovakia which prompted Hlouch and other ecclesial leaders such as Josef Beran to speak out against communist repression.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As Bishop of Budweis during a time of communist repression in Czechoslovakia, Josef Hlouch played a role in speaking out against communist authorities alongside other ecclesial leaders like Josef Beran. His actions contributed to the ongoing resistance against communist rule.
